title: Gare d'Austerlitz
visualBrief: The Seine clock pavilion and limestone wings frame the glazed historic hall. Iron lattice roof trusses and the Métro 5 crossing remain visible over the public concourse. The southern shed covers four mapped platforms and eight surface tracks.
nativeAxes: The 103.5 m mapped roof edge aligns the station axis toward the surface rail fan. Named Paris Austerlitz and Métro 5 features distinguish the terminal from the Seine and Muséum approaches.

materialMethod: Seven shared graphs supply limestone, weathered limestone, granite, painted iron, slate, standing-seam zinc and tinted glazing. The open hall uses an untextured translucent local material for its daylight panels.
limitations: The station shows the heritage envelope, restored hall and above-ground transport arrangement. Construction equipment, temporary diversions, underground levels and future retail changes are outside the modeled scope.
The 52-meter historic clear span follows SNCF documentation. Heights, façade recesses and the elevated Métro deck section are photo- and terrain-based reconstructions.
The fitted hall floor and station-end railway grades follow the standard viewer terrain approaches. The modeled elevated Métro deck covers the station crossing and its immediate ends.
